name: CT-04
label: Safe D

key_factors: Jim Himes is a well-established incumbent with a $2.5 million cash advantage over a challenger who has raised under $50,000
The district's partisan lean is D+13, giving Republicans little structural opening
Prediction markets price a Democratic win at roughly 98 percent
No public general-election polling exists, but no evidence points against the incumbent
model.rationale: Every available signal points the same way: a D+13 seat, a six-term incumbent who has raised roughly thirty times as much as his Republican challenger, no outside spending against Himes, and markets pricing his reelection near 98 percent. There is no evidence suggesting anything other than a comfortable Democratic hold.
model.watch: Only a major national Republican wave, an unexpected scandal, or late polling showing a dramatically closer race would warrant revisiting this rating.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Connecticut's 4th District leans Democratic by about 13 points, and Jim Himes has held the seat since 2009, building a profile of easy reelections. He enters the fall with roughly $2.5 million on hand after raising about $1.4 million this cycle, while Republican Michael Goldstein has raised under $50,000 and has no outside support on either side. A minor independent candidate also appears on the ballot but shows no measurable activity.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets put Himes's chances near 98 percent. With the incumbent unscathed by opposition spending and the challenger lacking resources, the expected margin sits in the low twenties, and the seat is rated Safe Democratic for 2026.
